in_hebrew.name: קרסימיר
in_hebrew.meaning: איש יקר, אדם חביב, שמח, מאושר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שם מקורו של יהודה - "שבח" - ו"י" - "אדם". בשם, שהתפתח במזרח האירופאי, נראה פירוש של "אדם יפה". בעיצוג רב-משמעי, זהו שם השייך לאדם בעל תכונות חביבות, שמחה ואושר, דבר שמחויב כאלקטרה. בפולקלור הסלאבי, קרסימיר תואר כנסיך חסר-דאגה, אשר תרם רבות לאדמתו ואישיו.

in_greek.name: Κρεσимиρ
in_greek.long_meaning: Απ' ό,τι φαίνεται, το όνομα Κρεσимиρ προέρχεται από την κριτική του ονόματος Κρέσος, που είναι συνδυασμός των κρητικά και το όνομα Σίμος, που σημαίνει ελαφρός. Ο Κρέσος ήταν τύραννος της Κρήτης το 69 π.Χ., που ήταν γνωστός για την ευγενεία και την φιλανθρωπία του. Στην συνέχεια, το όνομα Κρέσος συνδυάστηκε με το όνομα Σίμος, προσφέροντας στο όνομα Κρεσимиρ την σημασία του ευφραίνου.

in_latin.name: Kresimir
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Kresimir significat 'levem, facilem, felicem, beatum'. In linguistica Latina, nomen Kresimir derivatur a nomine Crisus, tyranni Cretae, qui erat notus pro sua liberalitate et humanitate. Crisus coniunctus est cum nomine Simus, quod significat 'levis'. Kresimir, igitur, significat 'felix, beatus', qui est persona grata et gaudentis.

in_english.name: Kresimir
in_english.long_meaning: The name Kresimir is derived from the Slavic name Krešimir, which is composed of the elements kri (light) and simir (happy or blessed). In Slavic mythology, Krešimir was a prince known for his kindness and generosity. In Christian tradition, the name Kresimir symbolizes a person who is blessed, happy, and easy to get along with, reflecting the qualities of a true Christian. In modern times, the name Kresimir has become popular in Eastern European countries, particularly in Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina.

historical_references.reference: Croatian King Kresimir IV (1058-1089 AD) was a ruler of the Croatian state during the High Middle Ages. He was the son of Petar Krešimir III and was the last independent ruler of the Croatian state before it came under Hungarian rule. He was known for his military successes and his religious patronage. He is considered a saint in the Croatian Catholic Church.

Saint Kresimir of Cetina (died around 303 AD) is the patron saint of Dalmatia and Split, Croatia. According to legend, he was a bishop in Salona (present-day Solin) and was martyred during the persecutions of Diocletian. His relics were later transferred to Split, where they remain venerated in the Cathedral of Saint Domnius.
